reason: I'll follow the blood through the filter first to see what passes through before the kidney recovers useful substances.
expectation: I expect small substances, including glucose, water, salts and waste, to pass through, while red cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the urine route, but I want to understand filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful substances through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube's arrows show useful substances returning to blood, matching the filtering and recovery goal.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving fluid that can become urine.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the route out, but I want to follow recovery first.

effect: Recovery returns useful substances and much water to blood, leaving a smaller volume containing wastes. I can now build the route out.
reaction: That makes the two-stage process clearer.
reason: The ureters lead from the kidneys toward the bladder, so I'll connect them first.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney pair, making a route toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also belongs in the urinary system, but the ureters connect directly to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are attached, leaving the bladder to complete the visible urinary organs.
reason: The bladder is the only offered combination and connects to the ureters.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach as a stretchy sac that receives urine from the kidneys.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the route where urine collects after passing through the ureters.
reaction: The explanation makes the tubes' destination clear.
reason: I'll follow the remaining kidney fluid into the assembled urinary organs before connecting them to the body.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to become urine and travel toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also meets a goal, but I want to finish following the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid follows the urine route to the bladder, while blood continues through a separate vessel. The filtering and recovery goal is complete.
reaction: Seeing the two routes stay separate makes the result clearer.
reason: Connecting the kidneys and bladder to the body is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the urinary organs to join the body model, with the kidneys connected to its blood supply.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body and its circulation, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The final picture clearly shows both the blood supply and the route out.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtering and recovery was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys need to take useful substances back rather than just filter blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was straightforward but less interesting as a choice because it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The filter lets glucose and other useful small substances through along with wastes, rather than picking out waste alone.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the pairings understandable, even when a fitting was straightforward.

continue.text: I would probably continue: following what happens to the filtered fluid made me curious about how other body systems work.
